feedback_rubric.title: Mock Interview Response Checklist
feedback_rubric.purpose: Help learners evaluate their own interview responses without requiring automated AI feedback.

rating_scale.label: Strong
rating_scale.description: The response clearly meets this criterion.

rating_scale.label: Developing
rating_scale.description: The response partly meets this criterion but could be clearer or more specific.

rating_scale.label: Needs Practice
rating_scale.description: The response does not yet meet this criterion.

checklist_items.label: The answer is organized.
checklist_items.description: The response has a clear beginning, middle, and ending.

checklist_items.label: The answer stays on topic.
checklist_items.description: The response directly answers the question asked by the interviewer.

checklist_items.label: The answer includes a specific example.
checklist_items.description: The response includes a real class, work, volunteer, project, or leadership experience.

checklist_items.label: The answer explains the learner's role.
checklist_items.description: The response makes it clear what the learner personally did.

checklist_items.label: The answer includes a result or lesson learned.
checklist_items.description: The response explains the outcome, impact, or learning from the situation.

checklist_items.label: The tone is professional.
checklist_items.description: The response uses respectful language and avoids oversharing unrelated personal details.

checklist_items.label: The answer connects to the job or employer.
checklist_items.description: The response helps the interviewer understand why the learner is a good fit for the role.

feedback_messages.message: Your response is strong. Continue practicing so your answer feels natural and confident.
Your response is developing well. Choose one area to strengthen, such as adding a specific example or explaining the result more clearly.
Your response needs more practice. Try using the STAR method and focus on one clear example.

best_practices: Practice out loud after writing your response.
Keep most interview answers between one and two minutes.
Use examples from school, internships, jobs, volunteering, student organizations, or class projects.
Do not memorize a script word for word. Practice key points so the answer sounds natural.
For visa or sponsorship questions, answer clearly and confirm details with a trusted campus or legal resource.
